title: Japan weekly: policy signals, revised credit data and October inflation
summary: 16–22 November: BOJ statements, retrospective housing-credit revisions and October CPI add context for borrowing decisions. They do not establish new bank mortgage rates or confirmed promotions.

takeaways.text: Separate policy views from decisions: Takata discussed flexible tightening; Ueda restated the October hold and a conditional adjustment path.
October CPI was released on 20 November. BOJ's 17 November credit notice also requires care with historical data vintages.
Existing monthly examples remain conditional; no newly confirmed bank promotion is established by this review.

sections.heading: 16 November: a member's policy assessment
sections.text: In his Tokushima speech, Hajime Takata argued for flexible, data-dependent adjustments rather than a predetermined interval or size of rate increases. He described his own assessment of inflation risks and the need to monitor financial conditions. This was a member's speech, not a new policy decision or lender announcement.

sections.heading: 17 November: housing-credit data revisions
sections.text: BOJ announced September lending data and retrospective corrections to some figures from June 2025 through June 2026. Affected series include housing-fund loans to individuals at domestic banks and shinkin banks. The notice does not quantify the corrections; their direction and magnitude are not established here.

sections.heading: 19 November: Ueda's parliamentary explanation
sections.text: Governor Ueda said the October meeting maintained an overnight policy target around 1.25%. Further adjustments depend on economic, price and financial conditions, with timing and pace assessed against the outlook and risks. This statement preceded the next day's CPI release and is not a response to it.

sections.heading: 20 November: October national CPI
sections.text: The Statistics Bureau reported October headline CPI up 2.3% year on year. Excluding fresh food, inflation was 2.2%; excluding both fresh food and energy, it was also 2.2%. The release uses 2025=100. These measure consumer-price baskets, not mortgage costs.

sections.heading: Earlier bank and funding-month context
sections.text: Mizuho's existing notice links borrowing by 31 March 2027 from 1.275% to July 2027 repayments from 1.525%, subject to further short-prime revisions and underwriting. JHF's November Flat35 example remains 2.81% for five years and 3.81% thereafter, assuming four discount points, LTV at most 90% and new JHF group credit life insurance. These pre-existing illustrations are not new weekly offers; Flat35's full-term schedule is fixed at funding.

sections.heading: What this means for a borrower
sections.text: Read the week's policy statements as context, not a rate forecast. For JPY variable borrowing, verify the contract's rate-reset and payment-review dates. For an initial fixed period, obtain the later pricing; for full-term fixed borrowing, confirm the funding month and every discount stage. Before using housing-credit trends, use consistently revised historical data rather than mixing vintages.

sections.heading: Unresolved package conditions
sections.text: This review does not establish individual JPY loan limits, term, residency or nationality eligibility, insurance, fees or guarantee charges, reward entitlement, early-repayment costs, or bank-specific five-year/125% payment rules. Those remain to verify. A public illustration is not a universal quote; no confirmed promotion record or automated-collection recovery claim is made.

sections.heading: Coverage and date meanings
sections.text: This retrospective covers 16–22 November in Asia/Tokyo and was written on 23 November. The coverage end is not an offer deadline. It synthesises events already covered in RatePro's individual reports without renewing them. Sources were re-read at the UTC times below. Mizuho's panel states 1 November; its first publication date is unknown. JHF states a November illustration, without a page publication date. The CPI URL is a rolling latest-release page; this report records its October edition.
